generated_by: merge of substances_part1.json (Agent B1) + substances_part2.json (Agent B2)
scope: All 5 modeled actives + losartan active metabolite EXP3174 + 37 excipients
disclaimer: RESEARCH SIMULATOR DATASET. Not a clinical decision tool, not medical advice, and not validated for patient care. Values are drawn from regulatory product labeling and published pharmacokinetic literature for the purpose of driving a mechanistic simulation, and several are explicitly marked ESTIMATED. Do not use to make prescribing decisions.

provenance_legend.wrapper: Every numeric pharmacological value is an object with keys: value, unit, range, cv_percent, n, distribution, provenance.

provenance.status.CITED: A real source states this value. source, url, quote (the value as the source words it), retrieved and tier are all populated.
provenance.status.ESTIMATED: Derived or assumed. provenance.note carries the one-line justification. No source/url.
provenance.status.NOT_FOUND: Searched and not found. value is null; provenance.note says what was looked for and where.

provenance.tier.1: Regulatory product labeling (FDA SPL via DailyMed/openFDA, EMA SmPC).
provenance.tier.3: Curated chemical/drug database (PubChem, ChEMBL, DrugBank, DrugCentral).
provenance.tier.4: Secondary web summary. Used only where tiers 1-3 failed, and marked as such.

provenance_legend.units: hours (_h), mg, ng/mL, L, L/h, mmHg, mmol/L. Fractions are 0-1 except fields named _percent.
provenance_legend.null_policy: null means absent. Never 0, never 'N/A'. Keys are never omitted.
provenance_legend.variability_policy: range and cv_percent are populated wherever the source supports them. Where a source gives mean +/- SD, cv_percent is computed as 100*SD/mean and provenance.note says so. Where only a min-max range is published, cv_percent is ESTIMATED by treating the range as an approximate 95% interval of a lognormal, and provenance.note shows the arithmetic.

provenance.note: THE headline variability number in this whole dataset — a 10-fold spread in F between individuals on the same dose. cv_percent=64 is ESTIMATED from the stated 6-60% span treated as an approximate 95% interval of a lognormal (sigma_log = ln(0.60/0.06)/(2*1.96) = 0.587 -> CV = sqrt(exp(sigma^2)-1) = 0.64). provenance.note: Unusually slow for an oral small molecule (contrast losartan at ~1 h). Driven by low passive permeability of a hydrophilic zwitterion and PEPT1-mediated uptake, not by any modified-release technology. The range shown is a reading of 'about 7 hours', not a separately cited interval.

provenance.source: FDA prescribing information, LISINOPRIL tablets (Solco Healthcare US, LLC), SPL set id 02c23f9c-f3cf-4366-ae1e-56296f1fedf9, effective 2026-05-22
provenance.quote: Upon multiple dosing, lisinopril exhibits an effective half-life of 12 hours.
provenance.note: EFFECTIVE half-life on multiple dosing — use this one for the simulation. The label separately warns of a 'prolonged terminal phase' representing saturable ACE binding that does NOT contribute to accumulation; do not use that terminal slope as the elimination t1/2 or the model will over-accumulate.

pk.terminal_half_life_note: Label: 'Declining serum concentrations exhibit a prolonged terminal phase, which does not contribute to drug accumulation. This terminal phase probably represents saturable binding to ACE and is not proportional to dose.' Modelling implication: a 1-compartment model with t1/2=12 h reproduces the clinically relevant exposure; the deep ACE-binding compartment is a PD effect, not a PK compartment.

provenance.note: No volume of distribution stated in the US SPL for adults. Only a qualitative statement that Vd 'appears to be slightly smaller' in heart failure. Needs a peer-reviewed source; not located within timebox.

Adult CL/F not stated in the US SPL. Label DOES give a paediatric anchor: 'The typical value of lisinopril oral clearance (systemic clearance/absolute bioavailability) in a child weighing 30 kg is 10 L/h, which increases in proportion to renal function.' Allometric scaling to 70 kg at exponent 0.75 gives CL/F ~ 10 * (70/30)^0.75 = 18.9 L/h; multiplying by F=0.25 gives systemic CL ~ 4.7 L/h. Flagged ESTIMATED — the derivation, not the number, is what to trust.

provenance.note: CL/F, 30 kg child. The 'increases in proportion to renal function' clause is the single most useful sentence in the label for a digital twin: it licenses CL_i = CL_pop * (eGFR_i / eGFR_ref) directly.

Derived, not measured: solving tmax = ln(ka/ke)/(ka-ke) for tmax=7 h (label) and ke=ln2/12=0.0578/h (label effective t1/2) gives ka=0.285/h. Both inputs are label-cited; the algebra is ours.
No lag time reported. 0.5 h assumed for gastric emptying of an IR tablet, consistent with tmax=7 h. Low impact on a 24 h simulation.

1-compartment with first-order absorption. Justification: the label's second (terminal) phase is explicitly attributed to saturable ACE binding and explicitly does not accumulate, so a second PK compartment would be modelling a PD phenomenon.

transporters: PEPT1/SLC15A1 (intestinal uptake — mechanistic attribution, see note)
metabolism.notes: NO CYP metabolism at all. This is why lisinopril is the simple baseline of the five-drug set: no enzyme-genotype axis, no CYP drug-drug interaction axis, no hepatic-impairment axis. Its entire personalization story runs through renal function alone. Label: 'Lisinopril does not undergo metabolism and is excreted unchanged entirely in the urine.' PEPT1 involvement is the accepted mechanistic explanation for its slow, saturable absorption but is NOT stated in the FDA label — treat as unsourced mechanism, not as a citable number.

provenance.source: FDA prescribing information, LISINOPRIL tablets (Solco Healthcare US, LLC), SPL set id 02c23f9c-f3cf-4366-ae1e-56296f1fedf9, effective 2026-05-22
provenance.quote: Impaired renal function decreases elimination of lisinopril, which is excreted principally through the kidneys, but this decrease becomes clinically important only when the glomerular filtration rate is below 30 mL/min. Above this glomerular filtration rate, the elimination half-life is little changed. With greater impairment, however, peak and trough lisinopril levels increase, time to peak concentration increases and time to attain steady state is prolonged
provenance.note: Label gives NO numeric AUC multiplier. The clinically operative threshold is GFR 30 mL/min: above it, model CL unchanged; below it, scale CL with GFR and expect a longer tmax as well. Dosing rule (label 2.4): CrCl 10-30 mL/min halve the initial dose; CrCl <10 or haemodialysis start at 2.5 mg.
No hepatic adjustment: lisinopril is not metabolised. Multiplier 1.0 by mechanism, not by study. This is a genuine differentiator versus losartan (5x) and amlodipine (1.4-1.6x) in the same dataset.

clinical_effect.dose_response_slope: Label-cited, qualitative but directionally firm: (a) 'An antihypertensive effect of lisinopril was seen with 5 mg of lisinopril in some patients. However, in both studies blood pressure reduction occurred sooner and was greater in patients treated with 10 mg, 20 mg or 80 mg of lisinopril than patients treated with 5 mg'; (b) from Dosage and Administration: 'Doses up to 80 mg have been used but do not appear to give greater effect' beyond the usual 20-40 mg/day range. So: steep between 5 and 10-20 mg, essentially FLAT from 40 to 80 mg. A saturating Emax curve with ED50 well below the usual dose is the right shape; a linear dose-effect term would be wrong at the top of the range.

provenance.source: FDA prescribing information, LISINOPRIL tablets (Solco Healthcare US, LLC), SPL set id 02c23f9c-f3cf-4366-ae1e-56296f1fedf9, effective 2026-05-22

provenance.note: NOTE THE PARADOX, it is a genuine finding and worth surfacing in the demo: BP effect begins at 1 h but plasma tmax is 7 h. Effect is not driven by plasma concentration in a simple direct-effect way — ACE inhibition in tissue precedes peak plasma levels. A direct-effect (no effect compartment) PD model will get the onset wrong.

provenance.quote: In hypertensive patients with normal renal function treated with lisinopril alone for up to 24 weeks, the mean increase in serum potassium was approximately 0.1 mEq/L; however, approximately 15% of patients had increases greater than 0.5 mEq/L and approximately 6% had a decrease greater than 0.5 mEq/L.

metabolism.notes: Losartan is best modelled as a PARENT-METABOLITE PAIR, not as a single drug. Sequence: oral dose -> ~33% systemic as parent (t1/2 2.1 h) -> 14% of the dose appears as EXP3174 (t1/2 7.4 h, 10-40x more potent). The engine needs two linked compartments with a formation-rate term, otherwise both the potency and the dosing interval come out wrong. Several inactive metabolites also form; they are not modelled.

provenance.note: *** DIRECTED AT AGENT D, WHO REPORTED THAT A LINEAR CYP2C9 ACTIVITY-SCORE MAPPING PREDICTS ONLY 1.14-1.35 FOLD FOR HETEROZYGOTES WHERE YASAR 2002 OBSERVED 2-3 FOLD. *** Use these OBSERVED values as a direct lookup table on the parent-to-metabolite AUC ratio and drop the linear activity-score model for losartan. The linear model underpredicts by roughly a factor of two at *1/*3 and by an order of magnitude at *3/*3, because CYP2C9-mediated activation is not linear in enzyme activity — it is a formation-rate-limited step in a sequential system, and the deficit is partly buffered by reduced metabolite clearance (which is exactly why Bae 2012 found E-3174 AUC 'not different' despite a clear change in the ratio). Lookup table: *1/*1 = 1.0 (reference), *1/*3 = 2.0, *2/*3 = 3.0, *3/*3 = 30.0, plus the ~1% non-converter phenotype where conversion falls from 14% of dose to <1%. *1/*2 was not separately reported by Yasar and is NOT_FOUND — do not interpolate it silently; if a value is needed, mark it ESTIMATED. IMPORTANT COUNTERWEIGHT: these fold-changes are on the parent/metabolite RATIO, and the 2021 meta-analysis found the underlying AUC effects significant in Asian subgroups but NOT in Caucasian subgroups, while Bae 2012 concluded clinical effect 'may not be reduced' in heterozygotes. So a large ratio shift does not automatically mean a large blood-pressure difference. Show the PK effect; do not claim a dosing consequence, since no CPIC or DPWG guideline exists for losartan.

Proxy populations differ substantially from one another, so the choice of proxy materially changes the answer and must be stated on screen wherever a frequency is shown. Two frequencies that ARE citable and are already in this file, both explicitly labelled by population: CYP2C9*2 12.5% and *3 8.7% in Turkish Behcet's patients versus *2 8.9% and *3 8.2% in Turkish healthy subjects (Goktas 2015, PMID 26233334); and CYP2C9*13 at 0.6% in Chinese healthy volunteers (Li 2009, PMID 19604036). The honest product behaviour is to let the user pick a reference population and show which one is in use, rather than to imply local data exists.

clinical_effect.dose_response_slope: STRONGLY SATURATING, and the label is explicit about it: '150 mg dose giving no greater effect than 50 to 100 mg'. Doubling 50 -> 100 mg buys very little additional BP reduction. The clinically useful lever above 50 mg is NOT dose escalation but either (a) splitting to twice-daily -- 'Twice-daily dosing at 50 to 100 mg/day gave consistently larger trough responses than once-daily dosing at the same total dose' -- or (b) adding a thiazide, which the label quantifies precisely: adding HCTZ 12.5 mg to losartan 50 mg gives 15.5/9.2 mmHg placebo-adjusted versus 5.5-10.5/3.5-7.5 for losartan alone. THAT PAIR OF NUMBERS IS THE BEST COMBINATION-THERAPY EVIDENCE IN THIS DATASET and should anchor Agent E's composition rule.

simulation_hooks.why_this_drug: The parent-metabolite drug. It forces the engine to model sequential compartments and gives the liver a visible role. Its genotype axis is the largest single personalization effect in the dataset (30x at *3/*3), and its bradykinin-neutrality is the cleanest mechanistic contrast against lisinopril.

substances.record_notes: STRONGEST parts: the label's Table 2 supplies mean +/- SD for AUC, Cmax, t1/2 and CLren in both parent and metabolite (N=12), so the CVs here are computed from cited data rather than assumed — the best variability data in B1's three drugs. The AUC consistency check (F x Dose / CL = 421 vs observed 442) independently validates the label's own numbers. WEAKEST parts: (1) logP and water solubility are both unresolved by orders of magnitude between DrugBank and HMDB — flagged, not silently resolved; (2) the label's Vd of 34 L is mutually inconsistent with its own CL and t1/2 under a one-compartment model, so a derived Vz of 109 L is supplied and the discrepancy documented; (3) the uricosuric effect, one of the stated reasons this drug is in the set, is NOT QUANTIFIED here and Agent C needs it before the gout contrast can be claimed; (4) adverse-effect incidence rates were not extracted within timebox. GENOTYPE CAVEAT: Yasar 2002 and Bae 2012 disagree — Yasar found large fold-shifts in the parent/metabolite ratio, Bae found E-3174 AUC 'not different' and concluded clinical effects 'may not be reduced' in *1/*3 heterozygotes. A 2021 meta-analysis found the effect significant in Asian but NOT in Caucasian subgroups. Report the disagreement; do not resolve it. And no CPIC or DPWG guideline exists for losartan (verified absent), so the product must not imply guideline backing.

metabolism.notes: EXP3174 is a terminal active metabolite — it is the end of the chain and is cleared renally (~50% of its clearance) and biliarily. It is FORMED by CYP2C9 (primarily) and CYP3A4 acting on losartan; it is not itself a CYP substrate of consequence in the label. Model it as: formation from the parent compartment at a rate scaled by CYP2C9 activity, then first-order elimination at 3.0 L/h.

provenance.note: Meta-analysis mean differences, not fold-changes. Direction is consistent: variant carriers have MORE parent and LESS metabolite. Crucially the effect was significant in ASIAN subgroups and NOT significant in CAUCASIAN subgroups for both AUC endpoints — relevant to a Central Asian deployment and worth surfacing rather than burying. See the losartan record's genotype block for the conflicting Yasar 2002 and Bae 2012 findings, and note that no CPIC or DPWG guideline exists. *** LOW CONFIDENCE — CONFLICTING PRIMARY EVIDENCE, DO NOT PITCH AS GUIDELINE-BACKED PERSONALIZATION. *** Yasar 2002 (PMID 11823761) and Sekino 2003 (PMID 14504849) find a genotype effect; Bae 2012 (PMID 22735459, n=43) finds E-3174 AUC 'not different' and concludes clinical effects 'may not be reduced' in *1/*3 and *1/*13; the 2021 meta-analysis (PMC8303964) finds the AUC effects significant in Asian but NOT in Caucasian subgroups. NO CPIC guideline and NO DPWG guideline exists for losartan/CYP2C9 (both verified absent by two independent agents). This is a PK observation with contested magnitude and no dosing recommendation attached — unlike metoprolol/CYP2D6, which has a 2024 CPIC guideline and CAN legitimately be pitched as guideline-backed. Display the disagreement; do not select the finding that tells the better story.

Since losartan RAISES angiotensin II (2-3x rise in renin activity), the parent progressively loses ground to the accumulating agonist while the metabolite does not. The 5.5-10.5/3.5-7.5 mmHg in the losartan record is the effect of the parent-plus-metabolite system and should be attributed to the pair, with the metabolite modelled as carrying the majority share.

substances.record_notes: This record exists to force the engine to model losartan as a parent-metabolite pair. Its PK numbers are as well-sourced as the parent's — the same label Table 2 gives mean +/- SD for AUC, Cmax, t1/2 and CLren (N=12), and its AUC CV of 26.8% is the tightest in B1's dataset. WEAKEST parts: no experimental physicochemical data of any kind exists (logP, pKa, solubility and melting point are all NOT_FOUND in PubChem PUG-View — only computed descriptors are available); no independent potency constant was retrieved, so the 10-40x weight-potency ratio from the label is all there is, and that range is four-fold wide; and the claim that the uricosuric effect belongs to the parent and not the metabolite is marked ESTIMATED and needs verification before the product relies on it.

substances.drug_class: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker (L-type, vascular-selective); third-generation, long-acting

identifiers.id_note: *** LABEL STRENGTHS ARE EXPRESSED AS THE FREE BASE, unlike losartan. *** A '5 mg' amlodipine tablet contains 6.94 mg of amlodipine besylate. Base fraction of the besylate is 0.7211 (5 / 0.7211 = 6.93 mg, matching the labeled 6.94 — conversion validated in research/physchem-identifiers.md). Katerzia oral suspension uses the BENZOATE salt instead (1 mg/mL amlodipine = 1.30 mg/mL amlodipine benzoate), a third salt form. Amlodipine is a racemate; the S-enantiomer carries essentially all the calcium-channel activity, and a marketed S-amlodipine exists in some countries but is out of scope here and is NOT modelled.

Moderate lipophilicity plus a basic amine is what gives amlodipine its enormous volume of distribution and consequently its very long half-life.

provenance.source: FDA prescribing information, AMLODIPINE BESYLATE tablets (Lupin Pharmaceuticals), SPL set id 003dd1ec-16f8-4f96-b6a8-c4689d35892a, effective 2026-04-20
provenance.quote: Within the physiologic pH range, amlodipine is an ionized compound (pKa=8.6), and its kinetic interaction with the calcium channel receptor is characterized by a gradual rate of association and dissociation with the receptor binding site, resulting in a gradual onset of effect.
provenance.note: *** THE MOST MECHANISTICALLY LOAD-BEARING SINGLE VALUE IN THIS RECORD, and it is stated in the FDA label itself. *** The primary amine is protonated at physiological pH; the resulting charged species associates with and dissociates from the L-type channel slowly. That slow receptor kinetics — NOT the plasma half-life alone — is why amlodipine has a gradual onset with no reflex tachycardia and why its effect outlasts its concentration. ChEMBL gives a basic pKa of 9.26 for the same compound; range spans both. Any PD model for amlodipine that assumes instantaneous receptor equilibrium contradicts its own label.

DrugBank DB00381 gives only the qualitative 'slightly soluble in water' for the free base, with no number. The besylate salt (the marketed form) is considerably more soluble, but no citable figure was retrieved. Not a blocking gap: amlodipine's oral absorption is high (F 64-90%) and is not dissolution-limited.

BCS I (high solubility as the salt, high permeability) is the usual assignment and is consistent with F 64-90% and logP 3.0 with no food effect. No FDA BCS assignment document was located, so this is marked ESTIMATED.

*** ESTIMATED, NOT LABEL-SOURCED — the most uncertain number in this record and flagged as such. *** The US SPL gives no volume of distribution (the only mention is 'weight-adjusted clearance and volume of distribution were similar to values in adults' in the paediatric section — a comparison with no number). 1470 L assumes the widely-quoted 21 L/kg at a 70 kg reference weight. Attempts to retrieve a primary or EMA source for 21 L/kg within the timebox failed (medicines.org.uk returned HTTP 404), so it is NOT presented as cited. INTERNAL CONSISTENCY CHECK supporting it: with Vd 1470 L and t1/2 40 h, CL = 25.5 L/h, and a 5 mg dose at F 0.77 gives Cmax ~2.6 ng/mL single-dose and ~7.6 ng/mL at steady state, both of which match commonly reported amlodipine concentrations. The three numbers hang together, which is evidence but not a citation. A ~1500 L volume of distribution — over 20x total body water — is what makes the half-life so long despite unremarkable clearance.

A simulation that only runs 24 hours will show amlodipine as far weaker than it truly is at steady state, by roughly the accumulation factor of ~2.9. The engine MUST either simulate to steady state or explicitly label a 24 h run as first-dose-only. This single fact justifies having a multi-day simulation horizon at all.

DERIVED: 1/(1 - exp(-ke x tau)) with ke = ln2/40 and tau = 24 h gives 2.94. Consistent with the label's stated 7-8 days to steady state (about 4-5 half-lives). Contrast losartan and lisinopril, which do not accumulate at all.

metabolism.notes: CYP3A4 substrate AND a weak CYP3A inhibitor — the interaction axis runs in BOTH directions, which is easy to miss and worth building into the rules engine. As a victim: diltiazem raises amlodipine exposure 60%. As a perpetrator: amlodipine raises simvastatin exposure 77% and cyclosporine troughs 40%. The label gives no quantitative data on CYP3A INDUCERS: 'No information is available on the quantitative effects of CYP3A inducers on amlodipine' — a genuine NOT_FOUND, verified rather than merely unfound.

clinical_effect.dose_response_slope: *** THE MOST IMPORTANT DOSE-RESPONSE FINDING IN B1's DATASET, and it is an ADVERSE-EFFECT finding, not an efficacy one. *** The label publishes dose-resolved oedema incidence (2.5 mg: 1.8%, 5 mg: 3.0%, 10 mg: 10.8%, placebo: 0.6%) but NO dose-resolved blood-pressure figures. Going from 5 mg to 10 mg roughly TRIPLES oedema incidence (3.0% -> 10.8%) while the label describes the BP gain only as 'dose-related', with no number. Efficacy rises sub-linearly and the visible adverse effect rises supra-linearly. This asymmetry is exactly what a dose-optimisation product should surface, and it is fully cited. It is also the strongest single argument for the product's core claim to recommend a BEST dose rather than a maximum one. A second, separately cited modifier: 'individuals with moderate hypertension (diastolic pressure 105 to 114 mmHg) had about a 50% greater response than patients with mild hypertension (diastolic pressure 90 to 104 mmHg)' — effect size scales with baseline BP, so the twin's starting blood pressure must modulate the response, and 'Normotensive subjects experienced no clinically significant change in blood pressures (+1/-2 mmHg)', which gives the model a cited zero at the bottom of the curve.

other_effects.mechanism: Label: 'Amlodipine is a peripheral arterial vasodilator that acts directly on vascular smooth muscle to cause a reduction in peripheral vascular resistance and reduction in blood pressure.' THE PRIMARY EFFECT AXIS. Note that amlodipine and lisinopril both lower BP by lowering resistance, but through entirely different molecular routes — direct calcium channel blockade in the myocyte versus removal of an endocrine vasoconstrictor. The organ animation should be able to show the same downstream change arising from two different upstream causes, which is a strong argument that the model is mechanistic.

adverse_effects.onset: Days to weeks; dose-dependent; often worse at day's end
adverse_effects.mechanism: Precapillary arteriolar dilation without matching venular dilation raises capillary hydrostatic pressure, forcing fluid into the interstitium. NOT fluid overload — this is why a diuretic does not fix it, and why adding an ACE inhibitor or ARB (which dilates the venular side) does. That is a genuinely useful positive recommendation the product can make: amlodipine + lisinopril or losartan reduces oedema relative to amlodipine alone.

simulation_hooks.why_this_drug: The long-half-life, hepatically-cleared, purely vascular drug. Its 30-50 h half-life and 7-8 day approach to steady state force the engine to handle multi-day horizons and accumulation, which the other two never exercise. Its oedema data is the only fully dose-resolved adverse-effect curve in B1's dataset and the most visually compelling thing to animate. And it is the counterexample on renal impairment: no adjustment, versus lisinopril's mandatory one.

substances.record_notes: STRONGEST parts: the dose-resolved oedema incidence table (1.8/3.0/10.8% at 2.5/5/10 mg with a 0.6% placebo rate) and the sex split (14.6% women vs 5.6% men) are the best-quantified adverse-effect data in B1's dataset; the placebo-corrected 12/6 mmHg standing BP reduction at 24 h postdose is the best-sourced efficacy number; the baseline-dependency multiplier (1.5x for moderate vs mild hypertension) and the cited near-zero effect in normotensive subjects (+1/-2 mmHg) give the PD model both a slope and a floor; and logP is confirmed at 3.00 by three independent sources. WEAKEST parts: (1) *** Vd and CL are both ESTIMATED and are the least certain numbers in this record *** — the US label gives no volume of distribution at all, the widely-quoted 21 L/kg could not be traced to a primary or EMA source within the timebox (medicines.org.uk returned HTTP 404), and CL is derived from it, so both inherit that uncertainty; they are internally consistent with the label's half-life and with commonly reported concentrations, which is corroboration but not citation. (2) No Cmax or AUC anchor exists in the label, so absolute concentrations are model-derived. (3) No numeric BP figures per dose level, so the efficacy dose-response shape is assumed while the adverse-effect dose-response is cited — an asymmetry worth stating openly. (4) No numeric exposure ratio exists for amlodipine with any STRONG CYP3A inhibitor in any label; the only quantitative evidence there is epidemiologic (AKI odds ratio 1.61) and must not be converted into an exposure multiplier.

provenance.quote: The dose of drug predicted to increase urate by 36 umol/L was 2.1, 8.9, and 12.3 mg for bendroflumethiazide, chlorthalidone, and hydrochlorothiazide, respectively.
provenance.note: CRITICAL FOR THE GOUT REJECT CASE: only 12.3 mg of HCTZ is needed to raise urate by 36 umol/L, whereas 26.4 mg is needed for a 10 mmHg SBP fall. In other words the urate harm appears at HALF the dose of the full BP benefit. HCTZ 12.5 mg is not a 'safe for gout' dose.

substances.record_notes: STRONGEST PARTS: the dose-response constants for BP, potassium and urate are all Tier 2 from one consistent meta-analysis (Peterzan 2012), so the harm/benefit trade-off across dose is internally coherent and is the best 'best dose' story in the whole dataset. WEAKEST PARTS: Cmax, Vd and blood:plasma ratio are Tier 4 and should be replaced. There is no published plasma concentration-effect relationship for HCTZ at all -- its effect is a function of tubular, not plasma, concentration -- so DO NOT build an Emax link from plasma concentration to BP for this drug. Drive HCTZ's effect from DOSE via the log-linear model, and use the PK only to animate the kidney and to time the diuresis. This is a genuine structural difference from the other four drugs and Agent E must know about it.

emax_model.form: fraction_of_max_beta1_blockade = C / (EC50 + C), C in ng/mL

Re-solving properly with a Hill model on the two points: 0.30 = 30^h/(EC50^h+30^h) and 0.80 = 540^h/(EC50^h+540^h) gives h = 0.68 and EC50 = 89 nmol/L = 23.8 ng/mL. So EC50 = 24 ng/mL with HILL COEFFICIENT 0.68, not 1.0. The shallow Hill slope is why a 4.9-fold exposure difference produces only a modest effect difference.

substances.record_notes: STRONGEST PARTS: (a) the CYP2D6 exposure ladder is Tier 2 from a 264-subject meta-analysis with four concordant parameters, and it cross-validates against the FDA label's independent poor-metabolizer half-life statement; (b) the label publishes an explicit plasma-concentration/effect curve (30-540 nmol/L -> 30-80% of maximal beta-1 blockade) AND an explicit beta-2 crossover threshold (300 nmol/L), which together let the simulator derive a real Emax model with a real safety threshold instead of inventing one; (c) the label states the concentration-effect relationship is formulation-independent, so one PD model covers IR and ER. WEAKEST PARTS: (1) the intermediate-metabolizer AUC multiplier (1.8x) is interpolated, not measured — CPIC explicitly declines to quantify it; (2) the blood-pressure effect size is ESTIMATED and the label itself says antihypertensive activity is NOT related to plasma level, so DO NOT let the demo claim a precise BP number for metoprolol — drive the story from HEART RATE, which is well characterised; (3) fraction metabolized by CYP2D6 (0.70) is B2's back-calculation; (4) ER Tmax is inferred from the Cmax ratio, not cited. DECISION RECORD: B2 modelled metoprolol as ONE moiety record with a salt_forms block and per-formulation PK, rather than as two substances. Reason: the PD is identical (label-stated), the moiety is identical, and splitting would duplicate the entire CYP2D6 block. The dose conversion between salts is captured in salt_forms[].free_base_fraction and MUST be applied when composing products.

patient_flag_definitions.lactose_intolerance: Contains lactose. Clinically relevant only for congenital lactase deficiency, galactosaemia or glucose-galactose malabsorption; ordinary adult lactose intolerance does not react to tablet-level quantities.

substances.formulation_implications: PATIENT-RELEVANT. Typical tablet lactose load is 50-200 mg. For context, most lactose-intolerant adults tolerate 12,000 mg (12 g) of lactose without symptoms, so a single tablet is ~100x below the usual symptom threshold. The clinically real exclusions are congenital galactosaemia, congenital lactase deficiency and glucose-galactose malabsorption — rare, absolute, and exactly the kind of narrow, correct rule a safety engine should encode instead of a blanket 'lactose intolerant -> reject'. Getting this nuance right is a differentiator; getting it wrong makes the product cry wolf.

substances.formulation_implications: PATIENT-RELEVANT (marginally). substances.formulation_implications: PATIENT- AND REGULATORY-RELEVANT, AND A GOOD PITCH DETAIL. TiO2 (E171) was banned as a FOOD additive in the EU from 2022 following an EFSA opinion that genotoxicity could not be ruled out; its use in MEDICINES was granted a transition because no drop-in replacement exists for opacification. The US retains it. So the same tablet can be legal in one jurisdiction and under review in another PURELY because of an excipient — a genuinely interesting point for a Ministry-of-Health audience and for Uzbek local manufacturing. B2 could not re-verify the current EU transition deadline within the timebox: DO NOT state a date in the demo.

substances.formulation_implications: THE HIGHEST-VALUE PATIENT-LEVEL EXCIPIENT FLAG IN THIS DATASET, and it lands on hydrochlorothiazide. Sunset Yellow is an AZO dye. FDA labelling for products containing FD&C Yellow No. 5 (tartrazine) requires a warning about allergic-type reactions including bronchial asthma, particularly in aspirin-sensitive patients; Yellow No. 6 is in the same chemical class and carries a recognised, if rarer, sensitivity signal. NOTE THE COLLISION WITH THE METOPROLOL ASTHMA CASE: an asthmatic patient can be harmed by the DYE in one product and by the ACTIVE in another. That is a genuinely sophisticated thing for the safety engine to show, and it is only possible because excipients are modelled as first-class substances. Not all HCTZ generics contain it — the ScieGen HCTZ tablet does not — so this is a product-level, not molecule-level, flag. That distinction is the whole argument for the Pills page.

cross_agent_notes.for_agent_B2_schema: Follow research/B1-notes.md section 1. Same Val wrapper, same provenance/tier keys, same units. Write data/substances_part2.json with the identical top-level shape; the lead concatenates the `substances` arrays.
for_agent_C_rules: Lisinopril + HCTZ potassium interaction is quantified in one trial, same units: lisinopril alone gives mean K+ +0.1 mmol/L with 15% of patients above +0.5; with HCTZ the mean flips to -0.1 with only 4% above +0.5 and 12% below -0.5. The cleanest drug-drug numbers in this dataset.

Amlodipine + simvastatin is a HARD DOSE CAP, not a warning: 'Do not exceed ZOCOR 20 mg once daily' (Zocor 2.5) and 'Limit the dose of simvastatin in patients on amlodipine to 20 mg daily' (Norvasc 7.7). Simvastatin AUC x1.77.

DO NOT create renal milligram caps for losartan or amlodipine. Both labels explicitly state no renal dose adjustment is needed, despite losartan exposure rising 50-90% in renal impairment. Only lisinopril has a real renal dosing rule (halve initial dose at CrCl 10-30; 2.5 mg below 10 or on dialysis).

POSITIVE rules available: amlodipine + beta-blocker is explicitly safe (no AV conduction effect, no adverse ECG changes in trials) — the product should say so rather than warn. Amlodipine + grapefruit juice has NO interaction per the label, so declining to warn is correct. Amlodipine + atorvastatin is fine while amlodipine + simvastatin is capped, so statin choice is a recommendable action.

Amlodipine effect is reported as similar in Black and white patients, whereas both RAAS drugs report a smaller effect in Black patients. Model via baseline renin status rather than a race checkbox — both labels supply the low-renin explanation themselves.

Losartan's uricosuric (urate-lowering) effect is NOT QUANTIFIED anywhere in B1's sources. It is a stated reason the drug is in the set and it anchors the contrast with HCTZ's gout reject case. Source a magnitude before writing that rule.

No CPIC or DPWG guideline exists for losartan/CYP2C9 or for amlodipine (both verified absent). Only metoprolol/CYP2D6 has one (CPIC 2024). Do not imply guideline backing for genotype-based losartan or amlodipine dosing.
for_agent_E_simulation: Losartan MUST be modelled as a parent-metabolite pair. The metabolite EXP3174 has t1/2 7.4 h vs the parent's 2.1 h and is 10-40x more potent; the parent alone cannot justify once-daily dosing.

The label volumes of distribution for losartan (34 L) and EXP3174 (12 L) are Vss and are mutually INCONSISTENT with the same labels' clearance and half-life under a one-compartment model. Derived Vz values of 109 L and 32 L are supplied in the records; use those for one-compartment work.

Peak-to-trough ratios span four orders of magnitude across B1's drugs: amlodipine 1.30, lisinopril 2.7, EXP3174 6.8, losartan parent ~2000. All derived from cited half-lives. This is the quantitative backbone of the concentration-time animation.

Amlodipine needs 7-8 days to reach steady state and accumulates ~2.9-fold; lisinopril and losartan reach steady state within a day and do not accumulate. A 24-hour-only simulation will materially understate amlodipine.
Lisinopril's PD onset is 1 h but its plasma tmax is 7 h. A direct-effect PD model cannot reproduce this; an effect compartment or turnover model is required.

COMBINATION ANCHOR, fully cited and in matched units: losartan 50 mg alone gives 5.5-10.5/3.5-7.5 mmHg placebo-adjusted; losartan 50 mg + HCTZ 12.5 mg gives 15.5/9.2 mmHg. The lisinopril/HCTZ label independently describes the combination as 'approximately additive'. Anchor the composition rule on these.
Amlodipine response scales with baseline BP (1.5x for moderate vs mild hypertension) and is near zero in normotensive subjects (+1/-2 mmHg). Use the normotensive figure as a boundary test.
Losartan's maximal effect takes 3-6 weeks to develop, so a purely concentration-driven model will over-predict day 1 and under-predict week 6. Relevant to the 5-year prognosis feature.
for_agent_F_organ_map: Best mechanistic contrast in the dataset: lisinopril LOWERS angiotensin II (blocks synthesis) while losartan RAISES it (blocks the receptor). Same BP outcome, opposite movement of the intermediate. Showing this proves the model is mechanistic rather than a lookup table.
Second best: the bradykinin/cough channel is lit for lisinopril (2.5% excess cough) and explicitly dark for losartan (label states it does not affect the bradykinin response).

Third: in the kidney, lisinopril dilates the EFFERENT arteriole and transiently LOWERS GFR, while amlodipine dilates the AFFERENT arteriole and RAISES GFR. Same organ, opposite direction, different arteriole.
Highest-impact adverse animation: amlodipine peripheral oedema, dose-resolved (1.8/3.0/10.8% at 2.5/5/10 mg) and sex-resolved (14.6% women vs 5.6% men). Bind ankle swelling directly to that curve.

None of B1's three drugs changes heart rate — all three labels say so explicitly (lisinopril 'no compensatory tachycardia', losartan 'essentially no change', amlodipine +0.3 bpm). Metoprolol is the only heart-rate actor in the set, so the heart animation's motion belongs to Agent B2's drug.
verdict_on_team_draft_scope_1_3: 'Lisinopril 5-40 mg' — PARTIALLY CORRECT. The 40 mg ceiling is right (label: doses up to 80 mg 'do not appear to give greater effect'), but the label's starting dose is 10 mg once daily; 5 mg is the start only for patients already on a diuretic, and the usual range is 20-40 mg/day.

'Losartan 25-100 mg' — CONFIRMED. Label: start 50 mg, maximum 100 mg, start 25 mg if volume-depleted or in mild-moderate hepatic impairment. The label adds that 150 mg gives no greater effect than 50-100 mg, so the cap is an efficacy plateau.
'Amlodipine 2.5-10 mg' — CONFIRMED exactly. Label: start 5 mg, maximum 10 mg, start 2.5 mg in small/fragile/elderly patients or hepatic insufficiency.

'Verapamil often avoided in heart failure' (step 3, item 3) — CONFIRMED and worth keeping, but note the corollary the draft does not state: amlodipine is NOT in that category. Its label documents no negative inotropic effect at therapeutic doses and no AV conduction effect even with beta-blockers, which is exactly why dihydropyridines are acceptable in heart failure while verapamil is not.
'ACE/ARB contraindicated in pregnancy' (step 3, item 8) — CONFIRMED. Both lisinopril and losartan carry BOXED WARNINGS for fetal toxicity. Two of the dataset's hard reject cases.

'ACE/ARB first-line and renal-protective in CKD' (step 3, item 2) — CONFIRMED in direction, but flag for Agent C: the labels do NOT support combining an ACE inhibitor with an ARB. VA NEPHRON-D (losartan + lisinopril, the exact pair in this dataset) was STOPPED EARLY for safety with no efficacy benefit — hyperkalaemia 6.3 vs 2.6 and acute kidney injury 12.2 vs 6.7 events per 100 person-years.

merge_note: Merged from two agent-owned files sharing schema v1. Part 1 (B1): lisinopril, losartan, exp3174, amlodipine. Part 2 (B2): hydrochlorothiazide, metoprolol, excipients. Source files retained for provenance.

provenance_legend_part2.wrapper: Every pharmacological numeric value is wrapped in the Val object defined in research/B1-notes.md section 1.2: {value, unit, range, cv_percent, n, distribution, provenance{status, tier, source, url, quote, retrieved, note}}. A bare number for a pharmacological quantity is a defect.

status.CITED: source + url + verbatim quote + retrieval date present
status.ESTIMATED: no source; `note` carries the one-line justification
status.NOT_FOUND: searched and not located; `note` records where B2 looked

tier.1: regulatory product labeling (openFDA /drug/label, DailyMed SPL) or clinical practice guideline (CPIC)
tier.4: secondary summary — used only where tiers 1-3 failed, and explicitly marked LOW CONFIDENCE

provenance_legend_part2.excipient_reduced_schema: Excipient records use the reduced schema permitted by B1-notes section 1.4. `pk` and `pd` are explicitly null rather than omitted — these substances have no modellable PK/PD. They carry instead: `excipient_function` and `excipient_functions_all`, `excipient_function_provenance` (ESTIMATED for all but magnesium stearate and talc, because the Handbook of Pharmaceutical Excipients and USP-NF <1059> are both paywalled), `max_amount_per_day_mg` (FDA Inactive Ingredient Database regulatory ceiling — a precedent limit, NOT a toxicity threshold), `typical_amount_mg` (NOT_FOUND for every excipient: quantities are trade secret and absent from both label prose and structured SPL), `present_in_products` with a per-product SPL setid citation, `patient_flags` with definitions, `patient_relevance` (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and `formulation_implications` prose.
provenance_legend_part2.salt_handling: Metoprolol is ONE substance record (the moiety) with a `salt_forms` block carrying the tartrate and succinate molecular weights and free-base fractions, and per-formulation PK in `formulations[]`. The PRODUCTS are separate records in data/products.json — metoprolol tartrate IR and metoprolol succinate ER are first-class distinct products with different approved indications. Rationale is in the metoprolol record_notes.
